criteria.criterion: Run cargo test --locked: a new test with a fake check runner whose check is killed at its deadline (exit code None, deadline note) shows the job ends closed as an environment stop (disk::is_environment_reason true on its reason, resumable_stop true), not Rejected; the test asserts this.
criteria.evidence: `a_check_killed_at_its_deadline_is_an_environment_stop` passed when I ran it. It runs the job through Athena::go, with a thread-local check seam returning exit_code None, a duration of 905 s and the production deadline_note. It asserts that the job state is Failed and not Rejected, that is_environment_reason and resumable_stop are true, that the verifier was called 0 times, and that the resume mark is at Checks. It then runs `athena retry` and asserts the retried job lands. Without the new branch in check_and_verify, the job would go on to the verifier and the Failed assertion would fail.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test --locked: a companion test shows a fake check that fails with a real nonzero exit code is still a failed check that leads to rejection, not an environment stop.
criteria.evidence: `a_real_failing_check_is_still_a_rejection` passed: with exit_code Some(1) after 905 s, the job ends Rejected with 'check probe failed', the reason is not an environment reason, the job is not resumable, and the verifier ran once. The checks.rs unit test `only_a_check_killed_at_its_deadline_is_timed_out` also passed. It runs the real runner and shows that a hung check counts as timed out, while exit 3, a pass, a skipped run, a start failure and the kill switch do not.

findings.summary: A timed-out job leaves no check record behind.
findings.evidence: Check runs are saved only inside the Verification record (line 1828). The new early return comes before that record is built, so the timed-out CheckRun (its output tail and number of tests run) is not kept. The duration and the limit do survive in the closing reason. The existing low-disk stop before the verifier works the same way.

findings.summary: A timeout in one check hides a real failure in another check of the same run.
findings.evidence: `check_runs.iter().find(timed_out)` turns the whole job into an environment stop even if a different check failed with a nonzero exit code. A retry will show that failure, so the cost is one extra round rather than a wrong verdict. A stricter rule would be to reject when any check fails for real and hold the job only when every failed check timed out.

findings.summary: The seam is consulted inside SnapExec::exec under cfg(test).
findings.evidence: This follows the existing replay_seam pattern and is compiled only for tests. Everything done with the returned run afterwards is the production code.

summary: The change passes. It does parts (1) and (2) of the request as the accepted reading defines them. athena.toml now sets check_timeout_s = 1800, and the schema in athena-data is unchanged. When a check is killed at its time limit, the job now closes Failed with an `environment: check timed out` reason instead of being rejected. The reason and the printed `failed` line show the measured time against the limit (for example '905s of 1800s limit'), the verifier does not run, and `athena retry` resumes the job from the checks stage. I ran the new tests in the snapshot and all passed: the job-level timeout test, the job-level test showing a real nonzero exit is still rejected, the unit test for the classifier in checks.rs, the reason test in disk.rs, and the test that loads the repository's athena.toml. fmt, clippy and the full test suite (1622 tests) passed in Athena's recorded checks. Telling a timeout apart from a failure reads the note that run_check itself writes, through a shared constant, and also requires no exit code, so it is sound. Two minor issues are worth a later fix. A timed-out job keeps no check record, because the early return comes before the Verification record. A timeout in one check also masks a real failure in another check until the retry. Part (3), the `athena status` duration report, is deliberately left to a follow-up job.
